newsitem.title: USA: Microdyne sees Q3 as "solidly profitable".
newsitem.headline: Microdyne sees Q3 as "solidly profitable".

text.p: Microdyne Corp said Tuesday it expected to be "solidly profitable" in the third quarter after reporting a net loss of $27.2 million or $2.11 per share for the second quarter.
"Our intention is to improve those earnings each quarter by increasing revenue and income at each of our divisions," it said.
The company, which makes communications equipment, said the loss for the second quarter ended March 30 included $26.6 million in costs to restructure one of its divisions.
For the same period the previous year, it reported a loss of $0.19 a share.

"We have taken the steps necessary to make the Networking Products Division profitable," it said, referring to the division it restructured. "Going forward, we expect the division to contribute to corporate earnings and cash flow. "Division expenses will be tightly controlled and will be pegged to revenue which, for the third quarter (ending June 29, 1997), we believe will exceed $10 million," it said.
The company said it would eventually decide whether to keep the division or divest it.
It also said it foresaw its operating divisions generating more than $12 million in cash this fiscal year.
"Coupled with our net loss carry-forward and sales of excess inventory, Microdyne could throw off up to $20 million of free cash over the next 12 months -- as much as $1.50 per share," it said.

"We have further reduced bank debt to under $8 million," it said. "As we begin to build cash in the coming quarters, we will have to choose among eliminating all bank debt, investing in attractive businesses, or retiring shares."
